internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 3 occurrences of frt is the same adjective furāt qualifying water. Twice (25:53, 35:12) it appears as the second predicate of the 'sweet' sea (ʿadhbun furātun) set against the salt-bitter sea (milḥun ujājun); once (77:27) it stands alone as the sole quality of the water God gives people to drink (māʾan furātan). Across all three, furāt marks water as fresh and drinkable — the opposite of undrinkable briny water. Whether furāt adds a specific nuance beyond ʿadhb (sweet) cannot be settled from the Quran alone, since the two are only ever co-predicated (25:53, 35:12) and the one solo use (77:27) shows furāt can carry the 'good drinking water' sense by itself but does not isolate its differential content.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: frt does NOT entail saltiness/bitterness (it is the explicit antonym of milḥ/ujāj in 25:53, 35:12); is NOT the noun for water/sea/river (māʾ and baḥr carry that — frt is only the predicated quality); does NOT by itself mean 'goes down smoothly/palatable' (that nuance is a separate predicate sāʾigh sharābuh in 35:12); carries NO motion/flow/'river' sense (25:53 and 35:12 describe standing sea-bodies, 77:27 water given to drink); is NOT applied to any referent beyond water/drink (0/3 non-water); and carries no negative, punitive, or neutral valence (every occurrence is in a sign/favour frame). No morphological or derivational spread beyond the single adjective (pure case variation only).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: None survives against the core sense: there is no occurrence where furāt attaches to non-potable, salty, or non-water referents, nor any with negative valence — the corpus is adversarially clean on 'fresh/drinkable water'. The residual weakness is precision, not consistency: in 25:53 and 35:12 furāt is co-predicated with ʿadhb, so it cannot be decisively separated from a mere near-synonym/emphatic doublet of ʿadhb; only the solo use in 77:27 pushes back by showing furāt can carry the sense alone, but 3 tokens in essentially one collocational frame cannot fix furāt's distinct differential content.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: furāt = simply 'sweet/fresh (of water)', a lexicalized near-synonym or intensifier of ʿadhb, the pairing ʿadhbun furātun being rhetorical emphasis rather than semantic addition. This account fits all 3 occurrences and cannot be eliminated Quran-internally; the 'distinct drinkability pole opposite ujāj' refinement rests on parallelism inference plus the single solo occurrence 77:27, which is suggestive but not decisive on 3 tokens.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: furāt = simply 'sweet/fresh (of water)', a lexicalized near-synonym or intensifier of ʿadhb, the pairing ʿadhbun furātun being rhetorical emphasis rather than semantic addition. This account fits all 3 occurrences and cannot be eliminated Quran-internally; the 'distinct drinkability pole opposite ujāj' refinement rests on parallelism inference plus the single solo occurrence 77:27, which is suggestive but not decisive on 3 tokens.
internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses (A, B, C) fully converge: a single ADJ lexeme furāt, one referent domain (water), one core value (fresh/drinkable, opposed to briny-bitter), zero resistant sub-class, zero counterexample. The evidence is internally consistent and adversarially clean, which supports a PREFERRED narrowest account. But STRONG requires broad, distinctive, adversarially-clean evidence: here the evidence is narrow and homogeneous (3 tokens, one form, effectively two environments — a doublet appearing twice plus one standalone), the item behaves as a lexicalized fixed epithet rather than a productive root, and the differential content of furāt vs ʿadhb is underdetermined internally. Per contract (CONSISTENT ≠ universally established; high frequency/consistency ≠ truth; narrow homogeneous evidence must not be over-graded; lexicalized class caps scope at REPRESENTATIVE), the honest ceiling is MODERATE + REPRESENTATIVE + LEXICALIZED_CLASS.

layer_attribution.derivation: No derivational spread: the root frt surfaces only as the adjective furāt, with pure case inflection and no verb or maṣdar; root-level generalization is not testable, so the claim is scoped to the lexicalized adjective.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Single lexicalized class — furāt as a fixed water-epithet meaning fresh/sweet and drinkable, the positive potable pole opposed to milḥ ujāj (briny-bitter).
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: In 25:53 and 35:12 furāt is contextually paired with ʿadhb and set against milḥ ujāj within a two-seas sign; in 35:12 the drinkability nuance is separately carried by sāʾigh sharābuh; in 77:27 furāt qualifies māʾ in a divine-provision drinking frame (asqaynākum). layer_attribution.reconciliation: No inter-lens conflict required reconciliation: Lenses A, B, and C converged on one consistent class and the same grade; no preliminary disposition was overturned.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: No distributional resistance and no resistant sub-class. hard_case_representation.rationale: There is no resistant, adversarial, or structurally atypical occurrence: all 3 tokens are one adjective, one referent (water), one consistent value, with zero counterexample. The only internal limitation is epistemic underdetermination of furāt's differential content vs ʿadhb, which is a precision gap (already recorded in strongest_counterexample/strongest_competitor and reflected in the MODERATE grade), not a distributional resistance. No occurrence is finally RESISTANT.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: An occurrence of frt (or the adjective furāt) predicated of a non-potable, salty/briny, or entirely non-water referent, or carrying a negative/punitive valence, or a Quran-internal environment that co-varies furāt against ʿadhb so as to fix a distinct differential content (or, conversely, collapse them) — any of which would break the 'fresh/drinkable water, opposed to briny-bitter' nucleus or its underdetermination claim.
rejection_condition.search_location: The 3 confirmed occurrences 25:53:7:1, 35:12:6:1, 77:27:7:1 and their full verse contexts; and any newly surfaced frt token beyond these three.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Re-read each verse_text for the referent frt modifies and its valence; check whether furāt ever attaches to non-water or salty referents, and whether furāt and ʿadhb are ever contrasted rather than merely co-predicated.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish furāt's own contribution from adjacent predicates ʿadhb (25:53, 35:12) and sāʾigh sharābuh (35:12); do not attribute the palatability/swallowability sense (sāʾigh) or the bare 'sweet' sense (ʿadhb) to furāt itself; exclude external lexica, tafsir, and any imported 'Euphrates/river/flow' reading not demonstrable in the packet.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If furāt is found on a non-potable/salty/non-water referent or with negative valence, the 'fresh drinkable water' nucleus is rejected; if an environment fixes furāt vs ʿadhb, the underdetermination note is resolved and the grade could move (up if a clean distinctive pole is shown, or toward synonymy if collapse is shown).

reopen_conditions: If any frt token is found predicating a salty/briny or non-water referent (breaking the milḥ/ujāj antonymy established at 25:53 and 35:12), reopen the 'fresh drinkable water' nucleus.

If a Quran-internal environment contrasts furāt against ʿadhb (rather than co-predicating them as in 25:53 and 35:12), or provides a second solo use beyond 77:27, reopen the underdetermined furāt-vs-ʿadhb distinctiveness and re-evaluate the MODERATE grade.
If furāt is found in a motion/flow/'river' or proper-noun frame, reopen the negative boundary excluding any flow/Euphrates sense.
